questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Leukonychia (white nails) points to hypoalbuminaemia, e.g. chronic liver disease; iron deficiency gives koilonychia (spoon-shaped nails).

options.label: B
options.explanation: Iron deficiency causes atrophic glossitis with a smooth, sore, red tongue from loss of papillae.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Iron is needed by rapidly dividing hair matrix cells; diffuse hair loss (telogen effluvium) is a recognised feature.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Angular cheilitis (cracks at the mouth corners) is a classic epithelial change of iron deficiency.

questions.pearl: Iron deficiency epithelial triad: koilonychia, glossitis, angular cheilitis; with a post-cricoid web it forms Plummer-Vinson syndrome.

questions.subject: Pediatrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: Marfan syndrome (FBN1 mutation) causes tall stature with long limbs and arachnodactyly.

options.label: B
options.explanation: 45,XO; SHOX haploinsufficiency gives short stature, treated with growth hormone.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Chronic protein-energy malnutrition and protein-losing states retard linear growth.

options.label: D
options.explanation: 47,XXY causes tall stature with eunuchoid proportions due to delayed epiphyseal fusion.

questions.pearl: Tall stature causes: Marfan, Klinefelter, homocystinuria, gigantism, constitutional; short stature: Turner, Down, hypothyroidism, GH deficiency, malnutrition.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Cotton wool spots (nerve fibre layer infarcts) are the hallmark of pre-proliferative (severe non-proliferative) retinopathy, not the defining PDR feature.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Microaneurysms are the earliest lesion and persist throughout all stages, including PDR.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Fragile new vessels on the disc or retina bleed into the vitreous, causing sudden painless visual loss in PDR.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Papilloedema is disc swelling from raised intracranial pressure, not a diabetic retinopathy feature.

questions.pearl: PDR is defined by neovascularisation (NVD/NVE); complications are vitreous haemorrhage, tractional detachment and neovascular glaucoma; treat with PRP or anti-VEGF.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Mycoplasma pneumoniae lacks a cell wall, so beta-lactams fail; it is the commonest atypical agent in young adults.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Chlamydophila pneumoniae and C. psittaci cause atypical pneumonia responding to macrolides or tetracyclines.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Klebsiella causes typical lobar pneumonia with red currant-jelly sputum, often in alcoholics.

options.label: D
options.explanation: E. coli causes typical Gram-negative (often nosocomial) pneumonia, not the atypical syndrome.

questions.pearl: Atypical pneumonia agents: Mycoplasma, Chlamydophila, Legionella, Coxiella; treat with a macrolide, tetracycline or quinolone.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: ECG changes in acute myocardial infarction:

options.label: A
options.text: Q wave greater than 2 mm in depth
options.explanation: Pathological Q waves (over 2 mm deep or 0.04 s wide, or over 25% of the R wave) indicate transmural necrosis.

options.label: B
options.text: Changes in leads II, III and aVF indicate inferior MI
options.explanation: Leads II, III and aVF face the inferior wall, usually supplied by the right coronary artery.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Absent P waves suggest atrial fibrillation or hyperkalaemia, not infarction itself.

options.label: D
options.text: R wave larger than S wave in V5
options.explanation: A dominant R wave in V5 is normal; the infarct-related dominant R appears in V1-V2 in posterior MI.

questions.pearl: STEMI evolution: hyperacute T waves, ST elevation, Q waves, then T inversion; dominant R in V1-V2 suggests posterior MI.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Ischaemia of the anterior segment disturbs lens nutrition, producing a complicated (secondary) cataract.

options.label: B
options.explanation: High degenerative myopia is a classic intraocular disease leading to complicated posterior subcapsular cataract.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Diabetic cataract is a metabolic cataract (sorbitol accumulation), classified separately from complicated cataract.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Long-standing retinal detachment causes complicated cataract with a polychromatic 'bread-crumb' posterior opacity.

questions.pearl: Complicated cataract follows intraocular disease: uveitis, high myopia, retinal detachment, retinitis pigmentosa, glaucoma; starts posterior subcapsular.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Topical beta-blockers reduce aqueous production and are part of initial pressure-lowering therapy.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Prostaglandin analogues act slowly via uveoscleral outflow and are not first-line in the acute attack.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Topical steroids control the accompanying anterior segment inflammation.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Pilocarpine constricts the pupil, pulling the iris away from the angle once IOP has fallen.

questions.pearl: Acute angle closure: IV acetazolamide, IV mannitol, topical timolol, pilocarpine and steroid, then laser peripheral iridotomy to both eyes.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Retained bile salts deposit in skin and cause itching.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Bile cannot reach the gut, so stools are pale (clay-coloured).

options.label: C
options.explanation: Water-soluble conjugated bilirubin spills into urine, making it dark.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Cholestasis raises conjugated bilirubin; unconjugated rise suggests haemolysis or Gilbert syndrome.

questions.pearl: Obstructive jaundice: dark urine, pale stools, pruritus, raised ALP and GGT; Courvoisier sign suggests malignant obstruction.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Binucleate 'owl-eye' Reed-Sternberg cells (CD15, CD30 positive) are diagnostic.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Bone tenderness over the sternum is a feature of leukaemia; alcohol-induced nodal pain is the classic Hodgkin oddity.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Hodgkin nodes are typically painless, rubbery and discrete, often cervical.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Although less common than in NHL, extranodal disease (lung, liver, marrow) occurs and denotes stage E or IV.

questions.pearl: Hodgkin lymphoma: bimodal age, contiguous nodal spread, B symptoms, Pel-Ebstein fever, alcohol-induced node pain.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: RAS encodes a GTP-binding signal transducer; point mutations lock it in the active state.

options.label: B
options.explanation: TP53 is a tumour suppressor ('guardian of the genome') that arrests the cell cycle after DNA damage.

options.label: C
options.explanation: EGFR (ERBB1) is a growth factor receptor tyrosine kinase; overexpression or mutation drives lung and other cancers.

options.label: D
options.explanation: PDGF receptor is a receptor tyrosine kinase proto-oncogene, e.g. mutated in some GIST.

questions.pearl: Oncogenes act dominantly (one hit); tumour suppressors (RB, p53, APC, BRCA) need both alleles lost (Knudson two-hit).

questions.subject: Gynecology
questions.stem: Causes of vaginal discharge with itching:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Candida causes curdy white discharge with intense vulval itching and soreness.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Trichomonas gives frothy greenish-yellow discharge with itching and strawberry cervix.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Gonorrhoea mainly causes cervicitis with mucopurulent discharge; pruritus is not typical.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Syphilis presents with a painless chancre, not an itchy discharge.

questions.pearl: Bacterial vaginosis: thin grey fishy discharge, pH over 4.5, clue cells, little itch; Candida: pH normal, itch prominent.

questions.subject: Pediatrics
questions.stem: Signs of good attachment during breastfeeding:

options.label: A
options.explanation: A wide gape allows the baby to take a large mouthful of breast and areola.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Body close to mother is a sign of good positioning, not attachment.

options.label: C
options.explanation: An everted lower lip is one of the four WHO signs of good attachment.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Supporting the whole body is a positioning sign, not attachment.

questions.pearl: WHO attachment signs: chin touching breast, mouth wide open, lower lip everted, more areola visible above than below.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences
questions.stem: Compared with the base, the apex of the upright human lung has:

options.label: A
options.explanation: The apex has a high V/Q ratio, so alveolar PO2 is higher (about 132 mmHg).

options.label: B
options.explanation: High V/Q at the apex washes out CO2, so PCO2 is lower than at the base.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Apical alveoli are already distended and less compliant, so they ventilate less than basal alveoli.

options.label: D
options.explanation: More negative apical intrapleural pressure keeps apical alveoli larger at rest.

questions.pearl: Both ventilation and perfusion are greatest at the base, but perfusion falls faster up the lung, so V/Q is highest at the apex; TB favours the apex.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Low oncotic pressure and renal sodium retention produce generalised oedema.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Serum albumin below 30 g/L follows urinary loss of over 3.5 g protein per day.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Hypertension is a nephritic feature; pure nephrotic syndrome (e.g. minimal change) is usually normotensive.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Hepatic lipoprotein synthesis increases in response to low oncotic pressure.

questions.pearl: Nephrotic: proteinuria over 3.5 g/day, hypoalbuminaemia, oedema, hyperlipidaemia, hypercoagulability (renal vein thrombosis).

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Essential hypertension results from polygenic susceptibility plus salt, obesity and stress.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Down syndrome is a chromosomal disorder (trisomy 21), not multifactorial.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Both type 1 and type 2 diabetes arise from multiple genes interacting with environment.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Obesity reflects polygenic predisposition combined with diet and activity.

questions.pearl: Multifactorial disorders: hypertension, diabetes, IHD, cleft lip/palate, neural tube defects, pyloric stenosis, congenital hip dislocation.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Ureteric calculi cause haematuria with severe colicky loin-to-groin pain.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Urothelial bladder cancer classically presents with painless frank haematuria.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Renal TB often gives painless haematuria with sterile pyuria and frequency.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Pyelonephritis produces loin pain, fever and dysuria.

questions.pearl: Painless frank haematuria in an adult is bladder cancer until proven otherwise; investigate with cystoscopy and CT urogram.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Robbins lists cell death (necrosis, apoptosis) as the response to severe or persistent injury such as ischaemia.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Fatty change is reversible injury with intracellular lipid accumulation, a listed response to metabolic injury.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Pathological (dystrophic) calcification is a recognised response to cell injury and death.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Hyperplasia is an adaptive response to altered physiological stimuli, part of the spectrum of cellular responses.

questions.pearl: Cellular responses: adaptation (hypertrophy, hyperplasia, atrophy, metaplasia), reversible injury (swelling, fatty change), cell death, accumulations, calcification.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: High-risk HPV 16 and 18 E6/E7 proteins inactivate p53 and Rb, causing cervical cancer.

options.label: B
options.explanation: EBV is linked to Burkitt lymphoma, nasopharyngeal carcinoma and Hodgkin lymphoma.

options.label: C
options.explanation: HIV is not directly oncogenic; malignancies arise indirectly via immunosuppression and co-infections.

options.label: D
options.explanation: HTLV-1 causes adult T-cell leukaemia/lymphoma through the Tax oncoprotein.

questions.pearl: Oncogenic viruses: HPV, EBV, HBV, HCV, HHV-8 (Kaposi), HTLV-1, Merkel cell polyomavirus.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Oral polio vaccine (Sabin) is live attenuated; IPV (Salk) is killed.

options.label: B
options.explanation: An intranasal live attenuated influenza vaccine exists alongside inactivated injectable forms.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Hepatitis B vaccine is recombinant subunit and standard hepatitis A vaccines are inactivated.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Rabies vaccines (cell-culture) are inactivated.

questions.pearl: Live vaccines: BCG, OPV, MMR, varicella, yellow fever, rotavirus, oral typhoid; avoid in pregnancy and immunosuppression.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Dry heat at 160 C for 2 hours sterilises glassware and powders.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Pasteurisation (63 C for 30 min or 72 C for 15 s) kills pathogens in milk but not spores, so it is disinfection, not sterilisation.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Inspissation at 80-85 C on three successive days sterilises protein-rich media such as Lowenstein-Jensen.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Moist heat at 121 C and 15 psi for 15 minutes kills spores; the standard sterilisation method.

questions.pearl: Autoclave biological indicator: Geobacillus stearothermophilus; hot air oven indicator: Bacillus atrophaeus (subtilis) spores.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences
questions.stem: Sites of erythropoiesis in the adult:

options.label: A
options.explanation: In adults red cells are produced in the red marrow of axial and flat bones.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The sternum is a flat bone retaining active red marrow, hence a marrow aspiration site.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The liver is the main site in mid-fetal life; in adults it is only extramedullary in disease.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Splenic erythropoiesis is fetal or pathological (extramedullary haematopoiesis, e.g. myelofibrosis).

questions.pearl: Sequence: yolk sac (to 2 months), liver and spleen (2-7 months), bone marrow (from 5 months onward).

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Carbamazepine typically causes diplopia, ataxia, hyponatraemia and rashes; dysgeusia is not a classic effect.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The sulfhydryl group of captopril causes taste disturbance (dysgeusia) and rash.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Frusemide causes electrolyte disturbance and ototoxicity, not taste loss.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Tetracycline is known for tooth discolouration, photosensitivity and GI upset rather than taste loss.

questions.pearl: Drugs causing dysgeusia: captopril, penicillamine, metronidazole (metallic taste), clarithromycin, lithium, griseofulvin.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences
questions.stem: Branches of the posterior cord of the brachial plexus:

options.label: A
options.explanation: The axillary nerve (C5-C6) is a terminal branch of the posterior cord.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The medial pectoral nerve arises from the medial cord.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The radial nerve is the larger terminal branch of the posterior cord.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Upper and lower subscapular nerves and the thoracodorsal nerve arise from the posterior cord.

questions.pearl: Posterior cord branches (ULTRA): Upper subscapular, Lower subscapular, Thoracodorsal, Radial, Axillary.

questions.subject: Pediatrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: Low metabolic rate and myxoedema cause weight gain despite poor feeding.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Myxoedematous infiltration of the vocal cords produces a hoarse cry.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Hypothyroidism causes bradycardia; tachycardia suggests thyrotoxicosis.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Untreated thyroid deficiency delays bone age and linear growth.

questions.pearl: Congenital hypothyroidism: prolonged jaundice, large tongue, umbilical hernia, constipation, wide posterior fontanelle; screen by heel-prick TSH.

questions.subject: Pediatrics
questions.stem: Causes of pathological jaundice appearing on the first day:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Rh isoimmune haemolysis produces rapidly rising jaundice within 24 hours.

options.label: B
options.explanation: ABO haemolytic disease is a common cause of jaundice on day one.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Physiological jaundice appears after 24 hours (day 2-3) and settles by day 7-10.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Jaundice of prematurity also appears after 24 hours and is more prolonged rather than early.

questions.pearl: Jaundice within 24 hours is always pathological: haemolysis (Rh, ABO, G6PD, spherocytosis) or congenital infection.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Digoxin increases ventricular automaticity and can precipitate or worsen VF.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Unstable angina is not a listed contraindication; digoxin is avoided in HOCM, WPW and heart block.

options.label: C
options.explanation: AF is an indication: digoxin slows AV nodal conduction to control ventricular rate.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Hypercalcaemia (like hypokalaemia) potentiates digoxin toxicity and arrhythmias.

questions.pearl: Digoxin toxicity: nausea, xanthopsia, bradycardia, bidirectional VT; worsened by hypokalaemia, hypercalcaemia, renal failure; antidote Digibind.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Corneal curvature is fixed; accommodation changes the lens.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Accompanying miosis cuts off peripheral rays, reducing chromatic and spherical aberration.

options.label: C
options.text: Refractive power of the lens is increased
options.explanation: Ciliary contraction relaxes zonules, letting the lens become more convex.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Pupillary constriction increases depth of focus, like a smaller camera aperture.

questions.pearl: Near triad: accommodation (lens convexity), convergence and miosis; ciliary muscle via parasympathetic oculomotor fibres.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: High urine specific gravity is found in:

options.label: A
options.explanation: ADH-driven water reabsorption produces small volumes of concentrated urine.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Reduced renal perfusion activates RAAS and ADH, concentrating the urine.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Failing kidneys lose concentrating ability, giving fixed low specific gravity (isosthenuria, about 1.010).

options.label: D
options.explanation: Tubulointerstitial damage impairs concentrating ability rather than raising specific gravity.

questions.pearl: High SG: dehydration, glycosuria (diabetes), contrast, SIADH, proteinuria; low SG: diabetes insipidus, CKD, overhydration.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Ageing slows cell proliferation, collagen synthesis and angiogenesis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Vitamin C promotes healing as a cofactor for collagen hydroxylation; its deficiency delays healing.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Reduced oxygen delivery impairs fibroblast activity and collagen synthesis.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Rest of the part favours healing; movement and tension delay it.

questions.pearl: Local delayers: infection (commonest), ischaemia, foreign body, tension; systemic: diabetes, steroids, malnutrition, age, anaemia.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Polyphenols in tea and coffee chelate non-haem iron and reduce absorption.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Ascorbic acid reduces ferric to ferrous iron and forms a soluble chelate.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Phytates in cereals form insoluble complexes with iron.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Sugars such as fructose form soluble iron chelates that enhance absorption.

questions.pearl: Iron is absorbed as Fe2+ in the duodenum via DMT1; hepcidin blocks ferroportin to reduce absorption.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Aminoglycosides damage cochlear and vestibular hair cells, often irreversibly.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Ethambutol causes optic neuritis with red-green colour blindness.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Loop diuretics alter endolymph ionic composition, especially with rapid IV dosing.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Tetracycline is not ototoxic, though minocycline can cause vestibular upset.

questions.pearl: Ototoxic drugs: aminoglycosides, loop diuretics, cisplatin, quinine, salicylates, vancomycin, erythromycin (high dose).

questions.subject: Obstetrics
questions.stem: Drugs used to manage hypertension in pregnancy:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Diuretics reduce the already contracted plasma volume in pre-eclampsia and are avoided.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Atenolol is associated with fetal growth restriction and is not preferred.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Labetalol (alpha and beta blocker) is first-line oral and IV antihypertensive in pregnancy.

options.label: D
options.explanation: ACE inhibitors are teratogenic, causing fetal renal failure and oligohydramnios.

questions.pearl: Safe in pregnancy: labetalol, nifedipine, methyldopa, hydralazine; avoid ACE inhibitors, ARBs, atenolol and diuretics.

questions.subject: Obstetrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: Eclamptic seizures threaten mother and fetus and need immediate magnesium sulphate and delivery planning.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Postpartum haemorrhage is a leading cause of maternal death and needs immediate resuscitation.

options.label: C
options.explanation: PROM needs assessment and planned management but is not itself an acute emergency.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Septic abortion is classed as a gynaecological complication of early pregnancy rather than a labour-ward obstetric emergency.

questions.pearl: Obstetric emergencies: eclampsia, PPH, APH, cord prolapse, shoulder dystocia, uterine rupture, amniotic fluid embolism, uterine inversion.

questions.subject: Obstetrics
questions.stem: Ultrasound in early pregnancy is done to see:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Placental site is assessed in the second and third trimesters, since a low placenta often migrates upward.

options.label: B
options.text: Diagnosis of congenital malformations of the fetus
options.explanation: First-trimester scan at 11-14 weeks detects anencephaly and nuchal translucency changes.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Early scan best determines number of fetuses and chorionicity (lambda vs T sign).

options.label: D
options.explanation: TVS showing an empty uterus with an adnexal mass and positive beta-hCG suggests ectopic pregnancy.

questions.pearl: Early USG: confirm intrauterine pregnancy, viability, gestational age (CRL most accurate), number and chorionicity, NT.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.stem: Minimum monitoring parameters in a shocked patient:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Base deficit is an advanced marker of tissue hypoperfusion, not part of minimum monitoring.

options.label: B
options.explanation: SpO2 is part of the minimum monitoring set with ECG and blood pressure.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Cardiac output monitoring is an advanced, invasive measure in ICU.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Hourly urine output (target over 0.5 mL/kg/h) reflects renal perfusion.

questions.pearl: Bailey minimum monitoring in shock: ECG, pulse oximetry, blood pressure, urine output; extended adds CVP, invasive BP, lactate, base deficit.

questions.subject: Pediatrics
questions.stem: Signs used to assess dehydration in acute watery diarrhoea:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Absence of tears is no longer used in the current WHO dehydration assessment.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Sunken eyes are one of the WHO signs for some or severe dehydration.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Slow skin pinch return (over 2 seconds = very slow) indicates severe dehydration.

options.label: D
options.explanation: CRT is a shock sign, not one of the WHO diarrhoea dehydration signs.

questions.pearl: WHO signs: general condition (lethargic/restless), sunken eyes, thirst (drinks eagerly/poorly), skin pinch; two or more decide the category.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Aspirin reduces thrombotic events in PRV.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Venesection to keep haematocrit below 0.45 is first-line therapy.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Hydroxycarbamide is cytoreductive therapy for high-risk patients.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Splenectomy is not a treatment for PRV and carries high risk; JAK inhibitors (ruxolitinib) are used for resistant cases.

questions.pearl: PRV: JAK2 V617F mutation in over 95%; aquagenic pruritus, plethora, splenomegaly, low EPO.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: TNF-alpha mediates fever, cachexia and granuloma formation.

options.label: B
options.explanation: IL-1 is a key macrophage-derived pyrogen and acute phase inducer.

options.label: C
options.explanation: IFN-gamma is produced by Th1 cells and NK cells; it activates macrophages rather than coming from them.

options.label: D
options.explanation: IL-17 is produced by Th17 cells to recruit neutrophils.

questions.pearl: Macrophage cytokines: IL-1, IL-6, IL-8, IL-12, TNF-alpha; IL-12 drives Th1, which returns IFN-gamma.

questions.subject: Pediatrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: Soft bones bend under weight-bearing, producing genu varum.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The white line of Frankel is a radiological sign of scurvy.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Cupping, splaying and fraying of metaphyses are classic X-ray signs.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Spinal deformities (kyphoscoliosis) occur in long-standing rickets.

questions.pearl: Rickets: craniotabes, rachitic rosary, Harrison sulcus, widened wrists, bow legs; raised ALP is the earliest biochemical marker.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Haemorrhage from thyroid isthmus or anterior jugular veins is a common early complication.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Upper airway obstruction is an indication for tracheostomy, not a complication.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Injury to the pleural dome, especially in children, can cause pneumothorax.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Respiratory failure is an indication; tracheostomy reduces dead space.

questions.pearl: Tracheostomy complications: haemorrhage, pneumothorax, surgical emphysema, tube block or displacement, tracheal stenosis, tracheo-innominate fistula.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Fluid of choice in dengue patients:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Isotonic crystalloid is recommended for plasma leakage in dengue.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Ringer's lactate (Hartmann) is an equally appropriate isotonic crystalloid.

options.label: C
options.explanation: DA solution is designed for diarrhoeal losses with extra potassium, not dengue leak.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Cholera saline replaces stool electrolyte losses and is not used in dengue.

questions.pearl: Dengue critical phase starts at defervescence; titrate isotonic crystalloid to haematocrit and urine output.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Persistent abdominal pain or tenderness signals plasma leakage.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Arthralgia ('breakbone fever') is a common febrile feature, not a warning sign.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Persistent vomiting is a WHO warning sign needing admission.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Retro-orbital pain is a classic early symptom, not a warning sign.

questions.pearl: WHO warning signs: abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, fluid accumulation, mucosal bleed, lethargy, liver over 2 cm, rising haematocrit with falling platelets.

questions.subject: Pediatrics
questions.stem: Causes of rectal bleeding in a child:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Haemorrhoids are uncommon in children but occur, e.g. with portal hypertension or chronic constipation.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Anal fissure from hard stools is the commonest cause of bright red bleeding in infants and children.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Intussusception gives red currant-jelly stool with colicky pain.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Juvenile polyps cause painless rectal bleeding, typically at 2-5 years.

questions.pearl: Painless massive rectal bleeding in a toddler: Meckel's diverticulum (Tc-99m pertechnetate scan).

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Rest pain, worse at night and relieved by dependency, marks critical ischaemia.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Paralysis is one of the 6 Ps of acute limb ischaemia, signalling an emergency.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Tissue loss (ulcer, gangrene) is the end stage of critical chronic ischaemia.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Absent or diminished distal pulses are a standard finding in chronic peripheral arterial disease.

questions.pearl: Fontaine stages: I asymptomatic, II claudication, III rest pain, IV ulceration or gangrene; ABPI below 0.5 suggests critical ischaemia.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Features of an upper motor neuron lesion:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Flaccid paralysis indicates an LMN lesion (or spinal shock).

options.label: B
options.explanation: Loss of descending inhibition causes spasticity (clasp-knife).

options.label: C
options.explanation: A Babinski sign reflects corticospinal tract damage.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Fasciculations occur with anterior horn cell disease (LMN), not UMN lesions.

questions.pearl: UMN: spasticity, hyperreflexia, clonus, extensor plantar, no wasting; LMN: flaccidity, areflexia, wasting, fasciculation.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Subdural empyema is an early, acute intracranial complication of the same infective process.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Gliotic scarring after abscess commonly leaves long-term seizures.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Ventricular rupture or meningeal scarring can obstruct CSF flow later.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Headache is the commonest presenting symptom, not a late complication.

questions.pearl: Brain abscess: commonest source is contiguous otitis media or sinusitis; ring-enhancing lesion on CT; avoid lumbar puncture.

questions.subject: Gynecology

options.label: A
options.explanation: Isthmic pregnancies especially rupture early, causing haemoperitoneum.

options.label: B
options.explanation: A tubal pregnancy is by definition an ectopic pregnancy, which may continue as such.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Perforation is not the term used; the tube ruptures rather than perforates.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Ampullary pregnancies often abort through the fimbrial end into the peritoneal cavity.

questions.pearl: Fates of tubal pregnancy: tubal abortion, tubal rupture, spontaneous regression, chronic ectopic, secondary abdominal pregnancy.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Raised oestrogen causes spider naevi in the SVC distribution; more than five is significant.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Koilonychia indicates iron deficiency; CLD gives leukonychia and clubbing.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Altered oestrogen-androgen balance and hyperprolactinaemia can cause gynaecomastia and galactorrhoea.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Onycholysis is seen in psoriasis and thyrotoxicosis.

questions.pearl: CLD hand signs: leukonychia, clubbing, palmar erythema, Dupuytren contracture, asterixis.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Insulin increases bone formation; diabetes is associated with reduced bone mass.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Oestrogen inhibits osteoclastic resorption; its loss causes postmenopausal osteoporosis.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Prolactin is not a principal regulator of calcium metabolism.

options.label: D
options.explanation: GH increases intestinal calcium absorption and stimulates bone growth via IGF-1.

questions.pearl: Main calcium regulators: PTH, calcitriol, calcitonin; also glucocorticoids (reduce), GH, oestrogen, insulin, thyroid hormones.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences
questions.stem: During spinal anaesthesia at L4-L5, structures traversed by the needle (posterior to anterior):

options.label: A
options.explanation: The needle passes skin, subcutaneous fat, supraspinous then interspinous ligament.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The needle pierces ligamentum flavum, epidural space, dura and arachnoid to reach CSF.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Pia is adherent to the cord and nerve roots and is not pierced; CSF lies superficial to it.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The filum terminale lies within the thecal sac among cauda equina roots and is not deliberately traversed.

questions.pearl: Spinal cord ends at L1-L2 in adults (L3 in neonates); the line joining iliac crests (Tuffier line) crosses L4.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Bowen disease is squamous cell carcinoma in situ.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Acanthosis nigricans is a marker of insulin resistance or internal (gastric) malignancy, not itself premalignant.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Leukoplakia is a premalignant white patch of mucosa, progressing to SCC.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Hidradenitis is chronic follicular inflammation; SCC only rarely arises in long-standing sinuses.

questions.pearl: Premalignant skin lesions: actinic keratosis, Bowen disease, leukoplakia, xeroderma pigmentosum, chronic scars (Marjolin ulcer).

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Cushing reflex causes bradycardia, not tachycardia.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Rising ICP produces systemic hypertension to maintain cerebral perfusion.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Raised pressure transmitted along the optic nerve sheath swells the disc.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Falling cerebral perfusion and brainstem compression depress consciousness.

questions.pearl: Cushing triad: hypertension (widened pulse pressure), bradycardia, irregular respiration; a late sign of herniation.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Hookworm is an intestinal nematode causing iron deficiency anaemia.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Pinworm is an intestinal nematode causing perianal itch; diagnose by cellophane tape test.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Schistosoma is a trematode (blood fluke), not a nematode.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Roundworm is the largest intestinal nematode; can cause obstruction and Loffler syndrome.

questions.pearl: Nematodes = roundworms; cestodes = tapeworms (Taenia, Echinococcus); trematodes = flukes (Schistosoma, Fasciola).

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Peptic or corrosive strictures cause progressive dysphagia to solids.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Iron deficiency underlies post-cricoid webs in Plummer-Vinson syndrome.

options.label: C
options.explanation: A large or retrosternal goitre can compress the oesophagus.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Barrett metaplasia is itself asymptomatic; dysphagia suggests complicating stricture or adenocarcinoma.

questions.pearl: Progressive dysphagia to solids then liquids in an older patient suggests carcinoma; dysphagia to liquids first suggests achalasia.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: IV calcium stabilises the myocardial membrane within minutes without lowering potassium.

options.label: B
options.explanation: ACE inhibitors reduce aldosterone and raise potassium; they should be stopped.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Nebulised beta-2 agonists shift potassium into cells via Na-K ATPase.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Insulin drives potassium into cells; glucose prevents hypoglycaemia.

questions.pearl: Hyperkalaemia: calcium gluconate (protect), insulin-dextrose and salbutamol (shift), resonium, diuretics or dialysis (remove).

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Morphine is the prototype mu-receptor agonist.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Thiopentone is an ultra-short-acting barbiturate IV induction agent.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Pethidine (meperidine) is a synthetic opioid; its metabolite norpethidine can cause seizures.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Fentanyl is a potent synthetic opioid about 100 times stronger than morphine.

questions.pearl: Opioid overdose triad: pinpoint pupils, respiratory depression, coma; reverse with naloxone.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: JNA causes recurrent profuse, often torrential, epistaxis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Extension into the orbit or pterygopalatine fossa causes proptosis and 'frog face'.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Eustachian tube obstruction leads to middle ear effusion and conductive loss.

options.label: D
options.explanation: JNA is histologically benign but locally aggressive.

questions.pearl: JNA: adolescent males, profuse epistaxis, nasal obstruction; Holman-Miller sign on imaging; biopsy is contraindicated.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Hypercalcaemia causes psychiatric 'moans': depression, fatigue, confusion.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Hypercalcaemia shortens the QT interval and predisposes to arrhythmias.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Hypercalciuria leads to calcium stones and nephrocalcinosis.

options.label: D
options.explanation: PTH-driven bone resorption causes osteoporosis and osteitis fibrosa cystica.

questions.pearl: Hypercalcaemia: bones, stones, abdominal groans, psychic moans; primary HPT shows high calcium with inappropriately normal or high PTH.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery

options.label: A
options.text: Commonest in the upper and inner quadrant
options.explanation: The upper outer quadrant is commonest because it holds most glandular tissue.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Combined OCP use carries a small increased relative risk while being taken.

options.label: C
options.text: Family history is a risk factor
options.explanation: First-degree relatives and BRCA1/2 mutations increase risk.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Nulliparity and late first pregnancy increase lifetime oestrogen exposure.

questions.pearl: Breast cancer risk: female sex, age, BRCA, early menarche, late menopause, nulliparity, HRT, obesity, alcohol.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Heterozygotes are unaffected carriers; disease needs homozygosity.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Autosomal disorders affect both sexes equally.

options.label: C
options.text: Needs two defective genes for expression
options.explanation: Both alleles must be mutated for the phenotype to appear.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Two carrier parents have a 1 in 4 risk per pregnancy of an affected child.

questions.pearl: AR diseases often enzyme defects: cystic fibrosis, thalassaemia, sickle cell, PKU, Wilson disease, haemochromatosis.

questions.subject: Gynecology

options.label: A
options.explanation: Mild septic abortion confined to the uterus is managed on the ward with antibiotics and evacuation; ICU is for septic shock.

options.label: B
options.explanation: It may progress to septic shock, DIC and renal failure.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Most infections arise from endogenous vaginal flora (anaerobes, E. coli) ascending into the uterus.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Foul-smelling discharge, fever and pain dominate; heavy bleeding is not the defining feature.

questions.pearl: Septic abortion: Clostridium welchii infection can cause haemolysis and acute renal failure; evacuate after starting antibiotics.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: A true cyst is lined by epithelium; a granulation or fibrous lining defines a false cyst.

options.label: B
options.explanation: A cyst is a collection of fluid in a sac lined by epithelium or endothelium.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Cysts contain secretions or transudate; an exudate-filled cavity is an abscess or false cyst.

options.label: D
options.explanation: A cyst under high tension may not fluctuate and can feel solid on palpation.

questions.pearl: True cysts are epithelium-lined; false cysts (pancreatic pseudocyst) have fibrous or granulation walls.

questions.subject: Gynecology

options.label: A
options.explanation: Friable malignant cervical tissue bleeds on contact; the classic presentation.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Cervical or vaginal endometriotic deposits can bleed after intercourse.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Fibroids cause menorrhagia rather than contact bleeding, unless a polyp is extruded.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Polyps, especially those protruding through the os, may bleed after coitus.

questions.pearl: Post-coital bleeding: cervical ectropion, cervicitis, cervical polyp, carcinoma; always visualise the cervix.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Appearance and behaviour open the MSE.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Thought form and content and perceptual disturbances (hallucinations) are core MSE domains.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Cognition, including orientation and memory, is assessed.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Gait belongs to neurological examination, not the mental status examination.

questions.pearl: MSE: appearance and behaviour, speech, mood and affect, thought, perception, cognition, insight and judgement.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: The patient points to the right iliac fossa as the site of maximal pain.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Murphy sign (inspiratory arrest on RUQ palpation) indicates acute cholecystitis.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Pressure in the left iliac fossa causes pain in the right iliac fossa.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Periumbilical bruising suggests retroperitoneal haemorrhage such as acute pancreatitis.

questions.pearl: Other appendix signs: McBurney point tenderness, psoas sign (retrocaecal), obturator sign (pelvic); Alvarado score aids diagnosis.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: TBM shows lymphocyte-predominant pleocytosis; neutrophils suggest bacterial meningitis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: AFB may be seen in the cobweb clot on Ziehl-Neelsen staining, though yield is low.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Protein is markedly raised in TBM, often over 1 g/L.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Glucose is low (CSF:plasma ratio under 0.5).

questions.pearl: TBM CSF: clear with cobweb clot, lymphocytes, very high protein, low glucose; basal exudates cause cranial nerve palsies and hydrocephalus.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Platelet function is normal, so bleeding time is normal; APTT is prolonged.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Haemophilia A (factor VIII) and B (factor IX) are X-linked recessive.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Males are affected; females are usually carriers.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Surgery including circumcision must be avoided unless covered by factor replacement.

questions.pearl: Haemophilia: haemarthroses and muscle bleeds; prolonged APTT, normal PT and bleeding time; desmopressin for mild haemophilia A.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Indian visceral leishmaniasis presents with massive splenomegaly; lymphadenopathy is uncommon (more in African disease).

options.label: B
options.explanation: CLL classically causes symmetrical generalised painless lymphadenopathy.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Primary syphilis gives regional inguinal nodes; secondary syphilis causes generalised lymphadenopathy.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Disseminated TB can cause generalised lymphadenopathy, though cervical nodes are commonest.

questions.pearl: Generalised lymphadenopathy: infections (EBV, HIV, TB, secondary syphilis, toxoplasmosis), lymphoma, CLL/ALL, SLE, sarcoidosis, drugs (phenytoin).

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: V/Q mismatch and hypoventilation desaturate arterial blood.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Pulmonary oedema impairs gas exchange, producing central (and peripheral) cyanosis.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Endocarditis causes fever, murmurs and emboli, not central cyanosis.

options.label: D
options.explanation: High haemoglobin makes 5 g/dL deoxygenated haemoglobin easier to reach.

questions.pearl: Central cyanosis needs about 5 g/dL deoxyhaemoglobin; visible on tongue; anaemic patients may not show cyanosis despite hypoxia.

questions.subject: Pediatrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: Surfactant deficiency causes hyaline membrane disease.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Preterms have little brown fat and large surface area, so hypothermia is the problem.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Low glycogen stores make hypoglycaemia the usual problem.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Hypothyroidism (including transient forms and delayed TSH rise) is more frequent in preterm infants.

questions.pearl: Preterm problems: RDS, hypothermia, hypoglycaemia, jaundice, NEC, IVH, PDA, ROP, apnoea, sepsis.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Flagella are the organs of bacterial motility.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Flagellar protein is the H antigen used in serotyping (e.g. Widal test).

options.label: C
options.explanation: Adhesion is the function of pili (fimbriae).

options.label: D
options.explanation: Flagella are made of the protein flagellin.

questions.pearl: Motility tests: hanging drop, Craigie tube; Salmonella H antigen detected in Widal; Proteus shows swarming.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Aspiration of water washes out surfactant and causes atelectasis and V/Q mismatch.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Hypothermia is a systemic feature, not a respiratory finding.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Surfactant loss and alveolar injury lead to ARDS.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Tachypnoea is non-specific and not a characteristic drowning finding.

questions.pearl: Drowning signs at autopsy: fine froth at mouth and nostrils, emphysema aquosum, weeds or mud in clenched hands, diatoms in bone marrow.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Hypothyroidism classically causes menorrhagia.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Increased peripheral resistance produces diastolic hypertension.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Reduced thermogenesis causes cold intolerance.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Reflexes show slow relaxation; brisk reflexes suggest hyperthyroidism.

questions.pearl: Hypothyroid ECG: bradycardia, low voltage; labs: high TSH, low T4, high cholesterol, raised CK, hyponatraemia.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Exanthematous skin rash is found in:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Measles gives a maculopapular rash starting behind the ears on day 4.

options.label: B
options.explanation: HHV-6 causes high fever followed by a maculopapular rash as fever falls.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Dengue produces a generalised maculopapular or confluent erythematous exanthem ('islands of white in a sea of red').

options.label: D
options.explanation: Morbilliform drug eruption is the commonest cutaneous drug reaction.

questions.pearl: Exanthem numbers: 1 measles, 2 scarlet fever, 3 rubella, 4 Dukes, 5 erythema infectiosum, 6 roseola.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.stem: Fluid choice for a burn patient in shock:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Ringer's lactate is the standard crystalloid for burn resuscitation (Parkland formula).

options.label: B
options.explanation: Hartmann solution is compound sodium lactate, identical in use to Ringer's lactate.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Large volumes of saline cause hyperchloraemic acidosis; it is not the preferred burns fluid.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Colloid such as plasma may be given after the first 24 hours (or in some protocols) to restore oncotic pressure.

questions.pearl: Parkland: 4 mL x kg x %TBSA of Ringer's lactate in 24 h, half in the first 8 h from time of burn.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Juvenile idiopathic arthritis is a classic cause of chronic anterior uveitis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: SLE can cause anterior uveitis as part of autoimmune ocular inflammation.

options.label: C
options.explanation: IBD-associated uveitis is HLA-B27 related and acute anterior.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Steroids treat uveitis; topically they may cause cataract and glaucoma.

questions.pearl: Acute anterior uveitis: HLA-B27 (ankylosing spondylitis, reactive arthritis, IBD); circumcorneal congestion, small pupil, KPs.

questions.subject: Obstetrics
questions.stem: Causes of bleeding in early pregnancy:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Hydatidiform mole presents with first-trimester bleeding and a large-for-dates uterus.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Ectopic pregnancy causes amenorrhoea, abdominal pain and slight vaginal bleeding.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Fibroids rarely cause bleeding in early pregnancy.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Abruption is an antepartum haemorrhage after 28 weeks, not early pregnancy.

questions.pearl: Early pregnancy bleeding: abortion (commonest), ectopic, molar pregnancy, implantation bleed, cervical lesions.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: A dense white line of provisional calcification at the metaphysis is classic.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Metaphyseal cortical defect (Pelkan spur, corner sign) is a scurvy radiological sign.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Defective osteoid synthesis produces generalised osteopenia with 'ground glass' bone.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Rachitic rosary (rounded costochondral swellings) is rickets; scurvy gives sharp scorbutic rosary.

questions.pearl: Scurvy: perifollicular haemorrhages, corkscrew hairs, bleeding gums, subperiosteal haemorrhage causing pseudoparalysis (frog-leg posture).

questions.subject: Pediatrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: Rubella causes arthralgia (especially in women) rather than myalgia.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Mild conjunctivitis accompanies the rash.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Meningitis is not a recognised complication of rubella.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Post-infectious encephalitis is a rare complication of rubella.

questions.pearl: Congenital rubella triad: cataract, sensorineural deafness, PDA; postauricular and suboccipital lymphadenopathy in postnatal rubella.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Furuncles are deep infections of hair follicles by S. aureus.

options.label: B
options.explanation: S. aureus, along with Streptococcus pyogenes, causes cellulitis.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Preformed heat-stable enterotoxin causes vomiting within 1-6 hours.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Exfoliative toxin cleaves desmoglein-1, causing superficial skin peeling.

questions.pearl: S. aureus toxin diseases: food poisoning, SSSS, toxic shock syndrome (TSST-1); coagulase positive.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: ANA positivity is characteristically found in:

options.label: A
options.explanation: RA is defined by RF and anti-CCP; ANA is only sometimes positive.

options.label: B
options.explanation: ANA is positive in over 95% of SLE, making it the best screening test.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Rheumatic fever is diagnosed by Jones criteria with ASO titre; ANA is not a feature.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Psoriatic arthritis is seronegative.

questions.pearl: SLE: ANA sensitive, anti-dsDNA and anti-Smith specific; anti-histone in drug-induced lupus.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.stem: Causes of otitis media with effusion:

options.label: A
options.text: Thick mucus plugging the tubal isthmus
options.explanation: Eustachian tube blockage creates negative middle ear pressure and transudation.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Allergic oedema of the tubal mucosa contributes to tubal dysfunction.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Adenoid hypertrophy obstructs the tubal opening, the commonest cause in children.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Viral URTI causes tubal oedema and is a recognised trigger of OME.

questions.pearl: OME (glue ear): commonest cause of hearing loss in children; flat type B tympanogram; persistent cases need grommets with or without adenoidectomy.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Ectatic scar lined by iris bulges forward after perforation.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Endophthalmitis or panophthalmitis following perforation can lead to a shrunken globe.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Descemetocele occurs before perforation, when only Descemet membrane remains.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Simple corneal scarring follows any healed ulcer; the perforation-specific scar is adherent leucoma.

questions.pearl: Perforation sequelae: iris prolapse, adherent leucoma, anterior staphyloma, anterior capsular cataract, endophthalmitis, phthisis bulbi.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Reduced renal clearance of prolactin causes hyperprolactinaemia in chronic kidney disease.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Oestrogen stimulates lactotroph prolactin secretion.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Chest wall and thoracic cord lesions stimulate the neural suckling reflex pathway.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Diabetes is not a cause of hyperprolactinaemia.

questions.pearl: Hyperprolactinaemia: prolactinoma, dopamine antagonists (antipsychotics, metoclopramide), hypothyroidism, CKD, pregnancy, stalk compression.

questions.subject: Pediatrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: Periostitis of the frontal bone produces frontal bossing (late congenital).

options.label: B
options.explanation: Painful osteochondritis causes Parrot pseudoparalysis in infancy.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Early congenital syphilis causes generalised lymphadenopathy and hepatosplenomegaly.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Infants cannot report pain; the bone lesions manifest as pseudoparalysis rather than bone pain as a feature.

questions.pearl: Late congenital syphilis: Hutchinson teeth, interstitial keratitis, eighth nerve deafness (Hutchinson triad), saddle nose, sabre tibia.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences
questions.stem: Type I collagen is found in:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Hyaline cartilage contains type II collagen.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Bone matrix is about 90% type I collagen; defective in osteogenesis imperfecta.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Tendons are dense type I collagen.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The annulus fibrosus of the disc is rich in type I collagen.

questions.pearl: Collagen types: I bone, skin, tendon; II cartilage, vitreous; III reticular, blood vessels; IV basement membrane.

questions.subject: Pediatrics
questions.stem: Causes of stridor in a neonate:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Laryngomalacia is the commonest cause of congenital stridor, worse on feeding and supine.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Adenoids enlarge after infancy and cause snoring, not neonatal stridor.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Retropharyngeal abscess can obstruct the airway in infancy, causing stridor.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Pneumonia causes tachypnoea and grunting rather than stridor.

questions.pearl: Neonatal stridor: laryngomalacia, vocal cord palsy, subglottic stenosis or haemangioma, laryngeal web, vascular ring.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Infection or tumours of the nasopharynx spread via the Eustachian tube.

options.label: B
options.explanation: A perforation allows external infection entry, causing recurrent otitis media.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Infected or enlarged adenoids block the tube and act as a bacterial reservoir.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Measles and scarlet fever cause necrotising otitis media.

questions.pearl: Children are prone to otitis media because their Eustachian tube is shorter, wider and more horizontal.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.stem: Motor nerve supply of the levator palpebrae superioris:

options.label: A
options.explanation: The ophthalmic nerve supplies sensation to the upper lid, not the levator muscle.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The maxillary nerve supplies sensation to the lower lid.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The superior division of the oculomotor nerve supplies the levator; palsy gives complete ptosis.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The optic nerve is purely sensory for vision.

questions.pearl: Müller muscle (sympathetic) adds 2 mm lid elevation; Horner syndrome causes partial ptosis, third nerve palsy complete ptosis.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences
questions.stem: Diseases under the International Health Regulations:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Plague is an IHR-notifiable epidemic disease.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Malaria is under WHO surveillance but not an IHR quarantinable disease.

options.label: C
options.explanation: HIV is not covered by the IHR.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Yellow fever is under IHR; vaccination certificates are required for travel from endemic zones.

questions.pearl: IHR (2005) always-notifiable: smallpox, wild polio, new influenza subtype, SARS; classic quarantinable: cholera, plague, yellow fever.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Otogenic brain abscess requires removal of the mastoid disease source.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Labyrinthitis complicating mastoiditis or cholesteatoma requires mastoid surgery.

options.label: C
options.explanation: CSOM with cholesteatoma (unsafe ear) is the commonest indication.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Parapharyngeal abscess is drained externally; it is not an indication for mastoidectomy.

questions.pearl: Unsafe CSOM: attic or posterosuperior marginal perforation, cholesteatoma, foul discharge; treat with modified radical mastoidectomy.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: ASOM causes primary otalgia from disease within the ear.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Peritonsillar abscess refers pain to the ear via the glossopharyngeal nerve.

options.label: C
options.text: Carcinoma of the base of the tongue
options.explanation: Referred pain via glossopharyngeal (and vagus) nerves is a classic warning sign.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Furuncle of the external canal is a primary ear cause of pain.

questions.pearl: Referred otalgia nerves: V (dental, TMJ), IX (tonsil, tongue base), X (larynx, hypopharynx), C2-C3 (cervical spine).

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Chronic suppurative lung disease is a classic cause of clubbing.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Cyanotic congenital heart disease causes clubbing.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Uncomplicated COPD does not cause clubbing; its presence suggests lung cancer.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Chronic suppurative lung disease in CF causes clubbing.

questions.pearl: Clubbing causes: lung cancer, suppurative lung disease, ILD, cyanotic heart disease, IE, IBD, cirrhosis; loss of Schamroth window.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.stem: Fluid for a patient after shock:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Cholera saline is formulated for diarrhoeal stool losses, not general shock maintenance.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Isotonic saline expands the extracellular volume.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Dextran is a colloid that expands plasma volume.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Dextrose normal saline provides sodium and some calories for maintenance after resuscitation.

questions.pearl: Crystalloids distribute across the ECF, so only about a quarter remains intravascular; colloids stay longer but carry anaphylaxis and renal risks.

questions.subject: Pediatrics
questions.stem: Clinical features of severe pneumonia in a child:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Fast breathing is the core sign of pneumonia and accompanies severe pneumonia.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Stridor at rest is a general danger sign classifying severe disease.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Wheeze suggests bronchiolitis or asthma rather than severe pneumonia.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Grunting reflects severe respiratory distress and is a sign of severe pneumonia.

questions.pearl: WHO fast breathing: 60 or more under 2 months, 50 or more at 2-12 months, 40 or more at 1-5 years.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Post-cricoid oesophageal webs cause dysphagia.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Iron deficiency causes angular cheilitis and glossitis.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Meckel diverticulum is unrelated to Plummer-Vinson syndrome.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Iron deficiency is central to the syndrome.

questions.pearl: Plummer-Vinson (Paterson-Kelly) syndrome is premalignant for post-cricoid squamous carcinoma; mostly middle-aged women.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Hypoxaemia is the core indication for supplemental oxygen.

options.label: B
options.explanation: High-flow oxygen speeds resorption of pleural air by lowering alveolar nitrogen.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Maximal oxygen is given during resuscitation.

options.label: D
options.explanation: 100% oxygen shortens COHb half-life from about 4-5 hours to about 1 hour.

questions.pearl: Target SpO2 94-98% in most patients and 88-92% in those at risk of hypercapnic respiratory failure (COPD).

questions.subject: Pediatrics
questions.stem: A 4-year-old boy has fever for 1 month, cough and weight loss. Investigations that help the diagnosis:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Chest X-ray shows hilar lymphadenopathy or infiltrates in childhood TB.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Blood culture helps exclude other causes of prolonged fever such as typhoid and bacteraemia.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Sputum (or gastric aspirate in young children) for AFB and culture or GeneXpert confirms TB.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Urine routine examination does not help diagnose a respiratory illness like pulmonary TB.

questions.pearl: Childhood TB: gastric lavage or induced sputum for GeneXpert, plus Mantoux and contact history; most children are smear negative.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Benign prostatic hyperplasia is hormone-driven proliferation of glands and stroma.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Physiological hormonal hyperplasia of glandular epithelium.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Skeletal muscle cells cannot divide, so exercise causes hypertrophy.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Cardiac enlargement involves hypertrophy and dilatation, not hyperplasia.

questions.pearl: Pregnant uterus shows both hyperplasia and hypertrophy; hyperplasia occurs only in cells capable of division.
